articles.summary: Synthetic opioids like fentanyl are more powerful and in plentiful supply, and they have transformed the drugs landscape.
articles.body:
America has been fighting the War on Drugs for decades, but the drug cartels, the suppliers and the dealers appear to be always one step ahead of the authorities.

President Trump has declared the cartels, "terrorists" and labelled fentanyl, the powerful synthetic opioid, a "weapon of mass destruction".

But the drug supply is changing, with other deadly synthetics being added to the mix, including strong animal tranquillisers, known on the streets as "tranq".

While overdose deaths are falling, the potency of the new drugs has recovery workers worried. For some the answer might lie in reducing demand, giving users support and helping them end their addiction.

articles.title: Asa de avião da Latam pega fogo antes da decolagem no Peru; passageiros desembarcam | G1
articles.standfirst: Incidente ocorreu no aeroporto de Lima, antes de voo com destino a cidade de Piura. Passageiros foram realocados e ninguém ficou ferido, segundo a companhia.
articles.summary: Incidente ocorreu no aeroporto de Lima, antes de voo com destino a cidade de Piura. Passageiros foram realocados e ninguém ficou ferido, segundo a companhia.
articles.body:
Um avião da Latam teve um problema técnico que provocou um incêndio em uma das asas antes da decolagem no Aeroporto Internacional Jorge Chávez, em Lima, no Peru , nesta segunda-feira (19). Os passageiros foram retirados da aeronave preventivamente. Ninguém ficou ferido.

O avião faria o voo LA2302, entre Lima e Piura, no norte do país. Segundo a companhia aérea, os protocolos de segurança foram acionados e o desembarque ocorreu conforme os procedimentos estabelecidos.

O Instituto Nacional de Defesa da Concorrência e de Proteção da Propriedade Intelectual do Peru (Indecopi) informou que acompanhou o atendimento aos passageiros no aeroporto. O órgão também verificou se a companhia fornecia informações claras sobre a mudança no horário do voo e os direitos dos clientes.

Imagens compartilhadas nas redes sociais mostram fogo em uma das asas do avião enquanto a aeronave ainda estava no solo.

Em um primeiro comunicado, a Latam classificou o caso como um evento técnico imprevisto e informou que as circunstâncias seriam investigadas.

Em uma segunda nota, a companhia informou que os passageiros foram transferidos para outro voo, que já havia pousado em Piura. A empresa não divulgou detalhes sobre a falha técnica que provocou o incêndio.

A Latam afirmou que ninguém ficou ferido e que as causas do incidente estão sendo investigadas.

A administração do Aeroporto Internacional Jorge Chávez informou que as operações continuaram normalmente após a ocorrência. Segundo o terminal, as duas pistas permaneceram em funcionamento, sem impacto nas chegadas e partidas de outros voos.

Motor de um Airbus A320 da Latam pega fogo durante a partida no Aeroporto Internacional Jorge Chávez, em Lima, no Peru. — Foto: Reprodução: X (@aviationbrk)

articles.title: Rio Grande em Colômbia SP: como é o rio onde jovens morreram | G1
articles.standfirst: Curso d’água nasce na Serra da Mantiqueira, percorre cerca de 1,2 mil quilômetros e é usado para geração de energia, abastecimento, irrigação, pesca e turismo.
articles.summary: Curso d’água nasce na Serra da Mantiqueira, percorre cerca de 1,2 mil quilômetros e é usado para geração de energia, abastecimento, irrigação, pesca e turismo.
articles.body:
Cheia do Rio Grande em Colômbia, SP — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O Rio Grande, onde uma caminhonete com três amigos caiu e afundou na madrugada de sábado (17), em Colômbia (SP) , é um dos maiores pontos turísticos da região. Ele nasce na Serra da Mantiqueira, em Minas Gerais, e percorre cerca de 1,2 mil quilômetros até se unir ao Rio Paranaíba e formar o Rio Paraná.

A bacia hidrográfica é formada por 393 municípios e 60,2% da área de drenagem fica em Minas Gerais, e outros 39,8% em São Paulo.

Segundo a Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo, o ponto onde a caminhonete afundou com os jovens, com idades entre 17 e 23 anos, tem aproximadamente cinco metros de profundidade.

A medida, no entanto, refere-se apenas ao embarcadouro da Orla Municipal de Colômbia e não representa todo o Rio Grande.

A profundidade e a força da água mudam ao longo do percurso. O rio também abastece um sistema com 12 reservatórios e é utilizado para geração de energia, abastecimento, irrigação, agricultura, criação de peixes, pesca e turismo. (entenda abaixo)

Ainda segundo a Defesa Civil, chovia em Colômbia no momento do acidente e a correnteza estava agitada.

Após a caminhonete cair dentro do rio, os três jovens conseguiram sair do veículo, mas dois deles acabaram arrastados pelas águas.

O corpo de Tiago Henrique de Matos Silva, de 23 anos, que dirigia o veículo, foi encontrado no domingo (18), nas proximidades da ponte entre Colômbia e Planura (MG). O corpo de Pedro da Silva Firmino, de 17, foi localizado na manhã de segunda-feira (19).

"Eu não sei nadar, sincero a falar, eu não sei nadar. Consegui ir flutuando até lá. Fiquei segurando nela [na bomba de captação]", contou.

Pescadores fazem buscas por jovens desaparecidos no Rio Grande, em Colômbia, SP — Foto: Reprodução/Defesa Civil

Profundidade e correnteza variam ao longo do rio

A profundidade do Rio Grande varia conforme o trecho. O fundo, a largura e o volume de água são influenciados pelo relevo, pelos afluentes, pelas chuvas e pelos reservatórios das usinas hidrelétricas.

No embarcadouro de canoas da Orla Municipal de Colômbia, onde aconteceu o acidente, a Defesa Civil estimou a profundidade em aproximadamente cinco metros.

A correnteza também não apresenta a mesma intensidade em toda a extensão. Na madrugada de sábado, chovia e a água estava agitada, segundo a Defesa Civil.

O órgão municipal também registrou vento, água turva e correnteza forte, e informou que as condições dificultaram o trabalho dos mergulhadores e reduziram a visibilidade dentro do rio.

Durante as buscas, pescadores se juntaram às equipes de resgate e percorreram as margens com canoas . Uma das embarcações utilizou um sonar para monitorar o fundo do rio.

Os voluntários também utilizaram uma espécie de gancho para tentar localizar objetos submersos. Quando algo era identificado, os bombeiros seguiam até o ponto para fazer a verificação.

A caminhonete foi localizada e retirada da água com a ajuda de uma escavadeira na tarde de sábado . As buscas pelos ocupantes mobilizaram equipes dos Corpos de Bombeiros de São Paulo e de Minas Gerais, das defesas civis estadual e municipal, da Polícia Militar e do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu).

Imagem mostra faróis da caminhonete brilhando dentro da água — Foto: Câmeras de segurança

O Rio Grande nasce em Bocaina de Minas (MG), na Serra da Mantiqueira, a aproximadamente 1,9 mil metros de altitude. Depois de percorrer cerca de 1,2 mil quilômetros, encontra o Rio Paranaíba na divisa entre Santa Clara d’Oeste (SP) e Carneirinho (MG).

A partir dessa confluência, os dois formam o Rio Paraná. Em parte do trajeto, o Rio Grande funciona como uma divisa natural entre Minas Gerais e São Paulo.

Na região de Ribeirão Preto e Franca , o rio banha ou delimita áreas de municípios como Rifaina , Igarapava , Miguelópolis , Guaíra e Colômbia.

Ao longo deste percurso, há trechos com características semelhantes às de grandes lagos, formados pelos reservatórios das usinas hidrelétricas.

A bacia hidrográfica reúne o Rio Grande e os cursos d'água que desembocam nele. Entre os principais afluentes estão os rios Aiuruoca, das Mortes, Verde, Sapucaí, Pardo e Turvo.

De acordo com a Agência Nacional de Águas e Saneamento Básico (ANA), a bacia ocupa aproximadamente 143,2 mil quilômetros quadrados e alcança, total ou parcialmente, 393 municípios, e aproximadamente 9 milhões de pessoas vivem nos municípios inseridos na bacia.

Buscas seguem no Rio Grande, em Colômbia (SP) — Foto: Câmeras de segurança

Ao longo do sistema do Rio Grande estão 12 reservatórios usados para geração de energia: Camargos, Itutinga, Funil Grande, Furnas, Mascarenhas de Moraes, Luiz Carlos Barreto de Carvalho, Jaguara, Igarapava, Volta Grande, Porto Colômbia, Marimbondo e Água Vermelha.

Na região de Ribeirão Preto e Franca, as usinas de Jaguara, Igarapava, Volta Grande, Porto Colômbia e Marimbondo transformaram diferentes trechos do rio em grandes reservatórios.

Nesses locais, o curso d'água se alarga e pode apresentar características semelhantes às de um lago. Em outros pontos, o rio passa por canais mais estreitos e pode ter correnteza mais intensa.

A ANA estabelece regras para a operação do sistema de acordo com o volume armazenado e os períodos seco e chuvoso. Além da geração de energia, as medidas precisam considerar outros usos da água, como abastecimento, irrigação e turismo.

A bacia também concentra indústrias, áreas de agricultura irrigada e parques aquícolas destinados à criação de peixes.

Em Colômbia, o Rio Grande faz parte da rotina de pescadores, moradores e visitantes. Segundo a Secretaria de Turismo do Estado de São Paulo, a pesca esportiva atrai turistas durante todo o ano.

O município conta com portos voltados à pesca, pousadas, barcos e serviços de piloteiros, profissionais que conhecem os percursos e acompanham os visitantes durante as atividades no rio.

A pesca esportiva, o turismo náutico e os eventos relacionados à atividade pesqueira estão entre as atrações oferecidas pela cidade.

A Orla Municipal, onde a caminhonete entrou na água, é utilizada para caminhada, lazer, atividades ao ar livre e acesso ao Rio Grande. No local também há um embarcadouro usado por canoas e outras pequenas embarcações.

Caminhonete retirada do Rio Pardo após acidente em Colômbia, SP — Foto: Kelven Melo/EPTV

Os três amigos, moradores de Indaiatuba (SP), estavam hospedados na região e voltavam para a pousada depois de passear pela cidade.

Segundo Lucas, o grupo viu uma área iluminada próxima ao rio e decidiu passar pelo local. Eles acreditaram que a rua contornava o Rio Grande, mas a via terminava no embarcadouro de canoas da Orla Municipal.

Em nota, a Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo informou que o motorista não percebeu o fim do trecho asfaltado. Por isso, a caminhonete entrou no rio pelo embarcadouro.

Lucas estima que o veículo estava a aproximadamente 45 km/h. Segundo ele, o amigo ainda tentou frear, mas não conseguiu parar antes de chegar à água.

Os vidros dianteiros estavam abertos, e os três ocupantes conseguiram sair da caminhonete. Lucas, que estava no banco traseiro, foi o último a deixar o veículo.

Tiago, que dirigia a caminhonete, foi levado pela correnteza. Segundo Lucas, Pedro tirou o calçado e o boné e mergulhou para tentar salvar o amigo. O adolescente conseguiu alcançar Tiago e tentou levá-lo em direção à margem.

Lucas disse que, já fora da água, procurou uma corda ou algum objeto que pudesse jogar aos dois, mas não encontrou. Ele acompanhou os amigos pela margem por cerca de 50 metros, mas caiu em pedras, machucou o pé e acabou perdendo os dois de vista.

"É uma coisa muito ruim a gente estar tendo que dar um depoimento desse. Eu queria que a gente tivesse nós três aqui falando isso."

articles.title: Cadu de Lula defende ampliação de investimentos na educação e na saúde | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PT fez caminhada na Zona Oeste de Natal e comentou o apoio do presidente da Assembleia Legislativa, Ezequiel Ferreira, anunciado no domingo (18).
articles.summary: Candidato do PT fez caminhada na Zona Oeste de Natal e comentou o apoio do presidente da Assembleia Legislativa, Ezequiel Ferreira, anunciado no domingo (18).
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte pelo PT, Cadu de Lula, fez uma caminhada nesta segunda-feira (19) pelo bairro Cidade da Esperança, na Zona Oeste de Natal . O ponto de encontro foi a Avenida Rio Grande do Sul. Acompanhado de apoiadores e correligionários e de deputados e vereadores do partido, o candidato conversou com moradores e ouviu reivindicações.

Cadu de Lula faz caminhada pelo bairro Cidade da Esperança — Foto: Inter TV Cabugi

Depois, seguiu em caminhada pelos bairros Cidade Nova e Felipe Camarão. Durante a agenda, Cadu falou sobre ampliação dos investimentos na rede estadual de educação e a proposta de ampliar o atendimento médico da rede pública de saúde por meio da telemedicina.

"Nós temos propostas para todas as áreas. Para a saúde, acesso a consultas a especialistas usando telemedicina, as centrais regionais de diagnóstico para acesso a exames de imagem, as cirurgias eletivas sendo realizadas nos hospitais regionais", falou.

No domingo, Cadu de Lula recebeu apoio do presidente da Assembleia Legislativa, Ezequiel Ferreira, do PSDB. O anúncio foi feito em uma rede social e aconteceu na sede do partido em Natal, junto com os deputados eleitos pelo partido, Gustavo Soares e Cristiane Dantas, além do deputado estadual Taveira Júnior, que não conseguiu renovar o mandato.

"Meus amigos do Rio Grande do Norte, reunião no PSDB, e uma decisão tomada por todos os parlamentares. Agora no segundo turno, vamos de Cadu governador do estado. No próximo domingo, ouvindo as nossas lideranças, ouvindo os nossos amigos, nós vamos para aquele que acreditamos ser o melhor gestor para o futuro do estado", comentou Ezequiel.

O candidato do PT também comentou a adesão do presidente da Assembleia. "O presidente Ezequiel, da Assembleia Legislativa, junto com os parlamentares do PSDB, aderiram à nossa proposta porque encontram aqui trabalho, honestidade, compromisso com o povo do nosso estado", concluiu.

articles.title: Incêndio em Ananindeua destrói casa no bairro Icuí-Guajará | G1
articles.standfirst: Família conseguiu sair do imóvel antes que as chamas se espalhassem. Segundo testemunhas, o fogo teria começado após um curto-circuito.
articles.summary: Um incêndio em Ananindeua destruiu uma casa no Icuí-Guajará após suposto curto-circuito, mas a família conseguiu escapar das chamas sem ferimentos.
articles.body:
Uma casa foi completamente destruída por um incêndio na noite de sábado (17), na rua Verão, no bairro do Icuí-Guajará, em Ananindeua , na Região Metropolitana de Belém. A família que estava na residência conseguiu sair a tempo e ninguém ficou ferido.

Segundo testemunhas, o incêndio teria começado após um curto-circuito na residência. As chamas se espalharam rapidamente e destruíram tudo o que estava dentro do imóvel.

Imagens que circulam nas redes sociais mostram a intensidade do fogo, que tomou conta da casa.

Uma equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionada e conseguiu controlar o incêndio. Segundo a corporação, a residência tinha três cômodos e sofreu perda total.

O Corpo de Bombeiros informou ainda que não houve vítimas e que o proprietário do imóvel optou por não solicitar perícia.

A causa do incêndio não foi oficialmente confirmada.

articles.summary: Raiara Nogueira faz parte do Corpo de Bombeiros Militar de Goiás. Nas redes sociais, ela mostra o como é o treinamento de militar e dá o recado: Viva sua vida normalmente!
articles.body:
A bombeira militar Raiara Nogueira emocionou internautas ao publicar registros que mostram sua rotina de treinamento militar em meio ao tratamento contra o câncer, em Goiás. Ao dividir o dia a dia da profissão nas redes sociais, ela demonstra força na preparação operacional e reforça um recado de otimismo para quem enfrenta desafios semelhantes: "Viva sua vida normalmente!" .

Em uma publicação nas redes no mês passado, Raiara escreveu: Vão te dizer que durante o tratamento oncológico você não vai conseguir fazer nada. Durante o vídeo, a militar mergulha em cachoeira, faz tirolesa, pega uma cobra e corre em praça.

articles.title: VÍDEO: capivara descansa entre jacarés na Transpantaneira em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo biólogo, o tamanho das capivaras e a disponibilidade de peixes ajudam a explicar o motivo dos jacarés nem sempre atacarem os roedores.
articles.summary: Capivara e jacarés no Pantanal aparecem juntos em vídeo; biólogo explica como o tamanho do roedor e a oferta de peixes influenciam o comportamento dos répteis.
articles.body:
🎥🐊 Uma capivara descansando ao lado de jacarés chamou a atenção de turistas durante um passeio pela Transpantaneira, no Pantanal. A cena foi registrada em 26 de agosto, durante o trajeto em direção a Porto Jofre, em Poconé , a 104 km de Cuiabá, e divulgadas recentemente nas redes sociais, (assista acima).

A guia de turismo Erica Moura fez o registro enquanto acompanhava visitantes da Espanha e do Chile. Segundo ela, a proximidade entre os animais surpreendeu o grupo e tornou a experiência marcante durante a viagem pelo Pantanal mato-grossense.

“O que se escutou ao redor é eles impressionados com a cena, dizendo que todo o esforço [da viagem] valeu a pena”, declarou.

Capivara descansa ao lado de jacarés às margens da Transpantaneira, no Pantanal de MT — Foto: Erica Moura

Ao g1 , o biólogo João Marcelo Biagini explicou que o tamanho das capivaras pode dificultar a captura. Alguns machos chegam a pesar entre 70 kg e 80 kg . Além do porte, os roedores têm dentes incisivos fortes e podem reagir a uma tentativa de ataque.

As capivaras também vivem em grupos, o que pode aumentar o risco para o predador. Ao tentar capturar uma adulta, o jacaré pode enfrentar a reação do próprio animal e de outros integrantes do grupo.

A disponibilidade de alimento também influencia esse comportamento, segundo ele. Durante o período chuvoso, quando há mais peixes, os jacarés encontram presas que podem ser mais fáceis de capturar do que uma capivara adulta.

“Tem grande disponibilidade de alimentação nessa época, tem mais peixe, então para eles é mais fácil pegar pegar, né, os peixes, porque os peixes são mais tranquilos, eles não atacam de volta”, explicou.

Apesar de a proximidade entre jacarés e capivaras ser comum de ser observada no Pantanal, isso não significa que os roedores estejam livres de ataques.

Segundo Biagini, durante a seca, a redução na disponibilidade de peixes e de outros recursos pode levar os jacarés a tentar capturar capivaras com mais frequência. Filhotes e animais doentes podem ser alvos mais vulneráveis.

“As capivaras pequenas, os filhotes, quando tem oportunidade, eles sim, eles pegam. E também as doentes”, detalhou.

Mesmo quando os animais aparecem lado a lado, portanto, não é possível concluir que não haja risco de ataque. O comportamento depende das circunstâncias e das condições encontradas pelo predador.

⚠️🐾Como as capivaras alertam outros animais

Já Erica explicou que as capivaras podem perceber rapidamente a aproximação de outros predadores, como a onça-pintada, por exemplo. Essa capacidade de reação pode servir de alerta para outros animais que estão por perto, como os jacarés.

“As capivaras percebem mais rápido a aproximação de grandes predadores terrestres, como a onça-pintada. A diferença na velocidade de reação é porque a capivara é uma presa pacífica e de sangue quente, enquanto o jacaré-do-Pantanal é um predador ectotérmico, de sangue frio”, acrescentou.

A cena registrada na Transpantaneira mostrou a proximidade entre as espécies, mas não significa que os roedores estejam sempre seguros e que não haja risco de ataque em outras situações.

articles.title: Masts from SS Richard Montgomery taken to Chatham dockyard
articles.summary: Removing the poles has reduced the risk of them toppling on to the bombs, a junior minister says.
articles.body:
Three masts removed from a bomb-laden shipwreck in the Thames Estuary have been successfully taken to a maritime museum.

The poles, delicately removed from the SS Richard Montgomery in September, will be kept at the Historic Dockyard Chatham.

The masts had been visible from the Essex and Kent coasts since the doomed vessel sank with 1,400 tonnes of explosives onboard in 1944.

Junior transport minister, Kier Mather said removing the masts had reduced the risk of them toppling on to and detonating the bombs.

"As the vessel has aged, the masts continued to place significant load on the structure," he said in a written statement to Parliament.

"Their removal has reduced that risk and supports the long-term safe management of the site."

A deadly secret in the Thames - what is the SS Richard Montgomery?

Engineers cut the masts free during a daring project , initially estimated to cost £9.5m. A crane supported the poles as they were sliced off and lifted to safety.

Mather said despite the "unique risk and a challenging site", the project was completed ahead of schedule and below forecast costs.

The BBC has asked the Department for Transport for details of the final costs.

SS Montgomery was loaded with 7,000 tonnes of munitions in 1944 and directed to anchor off Sheerness, Kent, but grounded on a sandbank.

Much of the cargo was removed, but the wreck remains in the sea and is visible about five miles away (8km) in Southend-on-Sea on a clear day.

Chatham Historic Dockyard will conserve the masts, following a campaign for them to stay in Kent , as they technically remained property of the US government.

The wreck remains subject to continuous monitoring and control via the exclusion zone in place.

articles.title: Neha Bora moves HC against police notice, likely to seek urgent hearing
articles.summary: Neha Bora challenges Delhi Police BNSS Section 126 notice in Delhi High Court, seeks quashing and protection from coercive action over alleged breach of peace.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora Monday challenged before Delhi High Court a police mandate asking her to execute a bond before a special executive magistrate for “keeping peace.”Bora, who has been at the forefront of recent protests against alleged irregularities in Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, is likely to seek an urgent hearing in HC as the matter is yet to be listed. Her petition seeks quashing of the notice and directions to the police not to take any coercive action against her.The notice, issued on Oct 17 under section 126 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), asked her to appear before the magistrate on Oct 19 and show cause why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety “for keeping peace for a period of enquiry.”As highlighted by TOI earlier, Section 126 empowers a a special executive magistrate to require a person to execute a bond for keeping the peace if there is credible information that he or she is likely to commit a breach of peace, disturb public tranquillity, or commit a wrongful act that may cause such a disturbance.Bora was taken into preventive detention on Oct 16 while she was on her way to participate in Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)’s ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march at Connaught Place’s Central Park. She was released a day later.In her plea, Bora argues the police notice is vague, factually incorrect and contains no material or information to substantiate the “likelihood” of breach of peace. It does not disclose a “period, occasion or event in relation to which breach is apprehended”, the plea argues, as it asserts that the proceedings are a “colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution”.The petition submitted that the proceedings initiated by police before the magistrate are based on alleged incidents of sloganeering at Mandi House on Oct 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under section 163 of BNSS, and instigating people to participate in a protest in CP on Oct 16. “The impugned notice rests on a prima facie incorrect fact, namely that the petitioner instigated people to participate in the demonstration at Central Park, CP on Oct 16. The petitioner’s call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House,” Bora’s petition said.“That the alleged disregard of ‘prohibitory orders 163 BNSS’ in the notice does not identify any specific prohibitory order and incident. articles.title: After ditching Mamata Banerjee, Yusuf Pathan gets a gift from Gujarat government
articles.summary: Gujarat govt approves allotment of disputed 978 sqm VMC Tandalja plot to Yusuf Pathan: 500 sqm as gift, 478 sqm sold at 55% of assessed value.
articles.body: VADODARA: The state govt has approved a proposal to allot a disputed 978 sqm Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) plot in Tandalja area to former India cricketer and ex-TMC MP Yusuf Pathan, with 500 sqm to be gifted to him for residential use and the remaining 478 sq metres transferred at 55% of the assessed valuation.VMC municipal commissioner Arun Mahesh Babu confirmed that the civic body had received the govt’s approval for the allotment sought by Pathan. “However, the details are yet to be finalised, and the proposal will have to go through VMC’s standing committee and general board approval process,” he said.The proposal will be considered by the Standing Committee before being placed for General Board ratification.The decision comes nearly two months after Pathan and other rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) Lok Sabha MPs broke away from Mamata Banerjee and announced their merger with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) on June 14, 2026, following BJP’s victory in the West Bengal assembly elections. Pathan was appointed one of the national vice-presidents of NCPI.The proposal, prepared by VMC’s land estate department, concerns a plot in Tandalja under town planning scheme 22, final plot 90. The land has an estimated market value of Rs 20.53 crore, based on a valuation of Rs 2.10 lakh per sq m approved by the civic body.Govt’s resolution reached VMC at the end of Aug. Pathan later withdrew his appeal before Gujarat High Court against the rejection of his earlier claim to the plot.Under the resolution, 500 sq m of the municipal land will be allotted to Pathan as a gift for residential use. The remaining 478 sq metres will be transferred at 55% of the valuation determined by the valuation committee of Vadodara Urban Development Authority (VUDA) on March 17, 2026, amounting to a 45% concession against that valuation.The resolution states that the arrangement will not set a precedent for similar cases. It also provides that the revenue department will allot VMC land equivalent in value to the land transferred to Pathan.The controversy dates back to 2012, when Pathan sought a 99-year lease of the plot adjoining his family’s residence. In his application, he cited security concerns arising from his profile as an international cricketer and said the adjoining land would be convenient for residential use.The standing committee and general board approved the proposal to allot the plot directly to him without a public auction and forwarded it to the state govt for approval. In June 2014, however, the urban development department rejected the proposal, citing the need for a public auction or open bidding for valuable land.The civic body subsequently alleged that Pathan had fenced and occupied the plot despite the rejection. The issue resurfaced in June 2024, days after he won the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when VMC issued him a notice directing him to remove the alleged encroachment.Pathan challenged the action before the high court. His lawyers relied on a govt policy concerning allotment of land to international sportspersons, while VMC argued that the plot belonged to the civic body and could not be allotted without following the prescribed procedure.In Aug 2025, the high court upheld govt’s rejection. The court held that prolonged possession without an allotment order or payment did not create a legal right to the land.Pathan subsequently appealed against the order. During hearings in June 2026, a division bench questioned how he had taken possession of public land without completing the allotment formalities or making payment. The court also cautioned that continued occupation could increase his financial liability.On Aug 31, Pathan withdrew his appeal unconditionally.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vadodara | Silver Rate in Vadodara | Bank Holidays in Vadodara | Public Holidays in Vadodara | Vadodara AQI | Weather in Vadodara | Petrol Price in Vadodara | Diesel Price in Vadodara | CNG Price in Vadodara | LPG Price in VadodaraStay updated with the latest Vadodara news. articles.title: Finland seeking one million land mines as it eyes Russian threat
articles.summary: Helsinki recently joined regional peers in withdrawing from UN Charter banning munitions as it eyes its eastern border.
articles.body:
Finland is seeking to acquire one million anti-personnel mines.

The plan to spend 100 million euros ($112 million) on the munitions comes after Helsinki and regional peers withdrew from a United Nations compact rejecting their use.

With Moscow increasingly accused of mounting hybrid warfare against supporters of Ukraine, and possibly planning military provocations, Finland exited the Ottawa Convention last year.

Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland, all also among the staunchest allies of Ukraine, also quit the agreement , citing the potential threat from Moscow.

Colonel Riku Mikkonen of the Army Command told Finland’s national news agency STT that officials are now gathering information from suppliers regarding the deal, the AFP news agency reports.

Helsinki would like domestic manufacturers to supply the mines, with contracts signed by the end of 2027 and production up and running by 2028.

“It would be useful in many ways if Finnish companies produced the anti-personnel mines in Finland,” Mikkonen said. About half a dozen Finnish firms qualify, he told STT.

“However, at this stage, buying the mines from abroad is not totally ruled out,” he added.

Finland joined the Ottawa Convention , a humanitarian treaty aimed at eliminating anti-personnel landmines and destroying more than a million of them, in 2012.

However, it announced that it was withdrawing in April 2025, citing a worsening security climate , and stopped being bound by the treaty in January.

Prime Minister Petteri Orpo has called Russia, which sits on Finland’s eastern edge, a long-term threat.

Finland shares a border of roughly 1,340 kilometres (830 miles) with Russia. It has beefed up its defences since Moscow’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and reported that migrants have been pushed across from the east .

Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen on Monday urged the EU to stop issuing tourist visas to Russians until the war ends.

“As long as Russia continues its invasion, Russian citizens should not be issued tourist visas,” she said, adding that it is “not right” for Russians to enjoy Europe’s freedoms “while their country bombs the homes of Ukrainians”.

Valtonen noted that Schengen countries granted nearly half a million tourist visas to Russians in 2025. Finland banned such visas in 2022, and she argued the rest of the bloc should follow suit.

articles.title: Carville says he'd rather Republicans keep the House than Democrats win by five seats, held 'hostage' by DSA
articles.summary: James Carville said he'd prefer Republicans keep the House by five seats rather than Democrats winning by five, becoming hostage to the DSA.
articles.body: Democratic strategist James Carville said during an interview on Sunday that he would rather the Republicans win by five seats in the House of Representatives in the midterm elections than the Democrats win by the same number, worrying that the Democratic Party would become "hostages" to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA). While speaking to "The Bulwark Takes," Carville provided his midterm election predictions, and said he would be disappointed if Democrats won by a slim margin. "I would be disappointed if it comes in at 225 House seats. And that would almost be — I would rather the Republicans keep the House by five than the Democrats win by five because if that happens, they're hostage to the DSA," Carville said. "Like Hakeem cannot move. There's no place for him to go. Even if you have a close Senate, Fetterman would keep Schumer [on] Pepto-Bismol all night. So, I think this is one of these races where margin matters a lot." STEWART EXPECTS SCHUMER, JEFFRIES TO DISAPPOINT IF THE DEMS WIN BACK THE HOUSE AND SENATE "Winning big is almost as big as winning, which is weird but it’s a nightmare at 225," he added. Bill Kristol, the host of "The Bulwark Takes," pushed back and said that was "a lower bound" for Democrats in the House. MAHER PREDICTS 'CLASSIC HISTORICAL A-- WHOOPING' FOR GOP IN MIDTERMS BUT WARNS DSA COULD HAUNT DEMS IN 2028 Moderate Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff pushed back on Carville's assertion in a statement to Fox News Digital. "I do think we have seen DSA figures overexploit their leverage to the point of sabotaging actual progress. One need look no further than the upcoming 10-year anniversary of Secretary Clinton losing to Donald Trump to find the data behind that claim. So I understand the concern, but Carville is absolutely wrong here and does a disservice to the vast majority of Democrats who absolutely want Democrats to win back the House and Senate, by any margin possible, to finally have a check on Trump’s radically anti-democratic agenda and the widespread corruption in his administration," he said. Shroff continued, "To suggest otherwise gives fodder to figures like Hasan Piker who claims Democrats are more against their farther left flank than MAGA — which is simply untrue. But when a figure like Carville makes this sort of statement, it goes viral and actually dissuades leftists in our big tent from even showing up. So it’s an irresponsible line from him." He argued that losing the House majority by five seats, as Carville suggested, was not the way to overcome the DSA's leverage. SOCIALISM SURGES AMONG DEMOCRATS AS PARTY LEADERS REJECT DSA AGENDA: ‘PACK OF FOOLS’ Carville also offered a behind-the-curtain take about the Democratic Party. "El-Sayed had AOC campaign with him on the Upper Peninsula," he said. "That doesn't make any sense." CARVILLE SAYS ONE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST'S 'LUNACY OF THE HIGHEST LEVEL' POLICY COULD HAUNT SWING-STATE DEMS "They had five progressive Democrats on the Upper Peninsula of Michigan," Carville continued to say. "What they're lining up to say is, 'You see that the moderate — the Clinton Democrats, like Carville, said they can only — all the DSA can win is in hardcore urban areas.' We have showed you that the people all over the country are waiting to be the sound of true progressivism." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE He said that progressives, such as Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., are setting themselves up to say that the progressive agenda could succeed anywhere in the country. JAMES CARVILLE WARNS FAR-LEFT CANDIDATES 'TOO HARD-HEADED' TO KNOW THEY'RE UNPOPULAR CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It's not. But it's not going to stop them from saying it. Trust me, that's what they're going to say," he said. Democrats are projected to take back control of the House and the Senate. The latest Power Rankings in the Senate point to Democrats and Republicans each taking 47 seats in the midterms, leaving six races rated as true toss-ups. Additionally, three races are rated as leaners — one step shy of a toss-up. These nine showdowns will likely determine whether the Democrats make a net gain of four seats to win control of the Senate or if the GOP holds the majority.

articles.title: In 1940, a Texas family acquired the ranch where generations grew pecan trees and spent holidays; 86 years later, they sold its 650 lakefront acres for more than $10 million so the land can become a state park
articles.summary: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation has bought a 650-acre waterfront ranch on Lake Palestine for more than $10 million.
articles.body: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation has bought a 650-acre waterfront ranch on Lake Palestine for more than $10 million. The purchase protects one of the largest remaining connected properties along the lake, with plans to turn it into a new state park. The property is in Henderson County, about 18 miles west of Tyler and 20 miles east of Athens. The Pollard family has owned the land since 1940. For decades, it was part of the family's business, Texas Pecan Nursery. It also served as a private retreat where family members gathered, hunted and fished. According to The Texas Tribune, the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation completed the purchase to hold the land temporarily until the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department formally buys it in late 2027.Acquisition structure and conservation fundingThe purchase follows a two-step process designed to make better use of public funds. The Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation will hold the 650-acre property until the state agency takes ownership. This allows the state to earn more interest on the voter-approved Centennial Parks Conservation Fund before using the money to complete the purchase. Texas voters approved the $1 billion conservation fund in 2023. The money is intended to help buy land for new state parks and pay for their development across Texas. Anne Brown, executive director of the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, explained why acting quickly was important when large properties become available. “Opportunities to protect a property like this don't come along very often, and when they do, timing is critical,” Brown said in statements quoted by The Texas Tribune. “TPWF was able to step in and secure this land now so it can ultimately become a place where generations of Texans can enjoy the outdoors.” Brown also said during a panel at the Texas Tribune Festival that partnerships with charitable organisations give the state more flexibility to secure land that could otherwise be bought by private developers for commercial use.Natural features and wildlife habitatThe Lake Palestine property has a range of natural features, including pine forests, native grasses, a working pecan orchard, a lake that reaches 58 feet deep and about 10 smaller ponds. The estate has roughly 2,000 feet of direct shoreline along Lake Palestine. It also provides a natural home for white-tailed deer, bobcats and native waterfowl. Real estate firm TexasLand handled the sale and represented the Pollard family. The process included nearly a year of site visits, environmental checks and inspections by state officials. Josh Smith, co-founder of TexasLand, recalled his first visit to the property. “The first time that I went out there, I thought, this place looks like a state park,” Smith told The Texas Tribune. “It just had that look.” Smith said officials from the state parks department inspected every part of the property during the year-long contract period before completing the purchase agreement.Family legacy and future public accessFor the Pollard family, selling the land to a conservation foundation means the property can remain undeveloped and eventually be opened to the public. “This land is part of my soul,” said Sam Pollard, president of Texas Pecan Nursery, in comments reported by The Texas Tribune. “It means a lot to me that we can leave a legacy for people to enjoy.” Rodney Franklin, director of Texas State Parks at the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department, welcomed the property as a new addition to the state park system. “We are excited to add this East Texas gem to the Texas State Park system,” Franklin said in a statement released by the agency. “Families will be able to enjoy lake recreation on Lake Palestine, along with the pecan trees that are a signature of the property. We are grateful to our partners, the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation, and to owner Sam Pollard and his family who have generously allowed this special slice of the Pineywoods to be accessible for generations of Texans.” The foundation now owns the property, but public access will be introduced in stages. After the state is expected to complete its purchase in late 2027, officials plan to begin with guided tours. They then plan to build permanent campsites, hiking trails, launch areas for paddling and facilities for day visitors. articles.title: Green Card ban: Tech firm Cloudera agrees to pay $2 million and accepts 2-year ban from PERM for discrimination
articles.summary: A California-based tech firm, Cloudera, has reached a settlement of $2 million with the Department of Justice and the Department of Labor on allegations
articles.body: A California-based tech firm, Cloudera, has reached a settlement of $2 million with the Department of Justice and the Department of Labor on allegations that the company discriminated against qualified US workers when it filed for Green Cards for its foreign workers. Additionally, the company will be banned from the Green Card process for two years. Cloudera's Green Card ban was announced earlier -- before the Donald Trump administration banned the Green Card process of eight major tech companies, including Microsoft and Adobe. Cloudera's case is different as there was a lawsuit filed against Cloudera in April this year.There are no exceptions: Harmeet K Dhillon“There are no exceptions: the Justice Department will hold accountable employers who discriminate against US workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This substantial settlement, in partnership with DOL, sends a strong signal to employers that the federal government will work together to ensure employers treat US workers fairly.”In April, DOJ filed a lawsuit alleging that Cloudera alleging that the company violated the Immigration and Nationality Act by discriminating against US workers "when recruiting and hiring for seven positions under the PERM process".The Justice Department said that under the terms of the settlement,, Cloudera will establish a back-pay fund of $1.4 million to compensate qualified US workers who tried to apply for the jobs at issue but were not given fair consideration. Cloudera will also pay $600,000 in civil penalties to the United States."Cloudera will be subject to compliance obligations designed to ensure future adherence to federal labor and anti-discrimination laws. These measures include enhanced monitoring, revised PERM compliance procedures, and reporting requirements intended to prevent future violations," the department said.The PERM (Program Electronic Review Management) process is the mandatory first step for US employers sponsoring a foreign national for an employment-based green card (typically EB-2 or EB-3). It is designed to prove to the US Department of Labor (DOL) that there are no qualified, willing, and available US workers for the job, and that hiring the foreign worker will not lower local wages. articles.title: Woman wins $1,800 wrongful eviction award despite not being named on the lease; Louisiana court says occupants still have legal protections
articles.summary: A woman in New Orleans was awarded $1,800 after a court upheld a wrongful eviction ruling, despite her not being the named tenant on the lease.
articles.body: A woman in New Orleans was awarded $1,800 after a court upheld a wrongful eviction ruling, despite her not being the named tenant on the lease. Joddice Taylor was ordered to leave her home after the death of her long-time partner, Nelson Ragas, without being allowed to take her belongings. According to the Louisiana Fourth Circuit Court of Appeal, which ruled on 19 May 2026, the property manager had failed to follow the required legal procedures before removing her. The court confirmed that occupants can receive eviction protections similar to tenants, even when they are not named on the lease.Woman wins $1,800 despite not being a tenantTaylor and Ragas had lived together for approximately 15 years and shared the apartment at Guste Homes in New Orleans for around three years. Ragas was the tenant under the lease, while Taylor had signed an addendum identifying herself as his live-in aide. The agreement stated that her right to remain in the apartment depended on Ragas continuing to employ her and that she would have to leave if he died or moved out of the subsidised housing programme.On 3 January 2022, Taylor delivered Ragas' rent cheque to Guste Homes Resident Management Corporation. Ragas died later that day. According to Taylor, she informed the property’s manager, Wilson, of his death on 5 January, though Wilson was already aware of it. He initially told her that she needed to vacate the apartment within three weeks. However, Taylor testified that Wilson met her at the apartment later that day, accompanied by another employee, and ordered her to leave immediately. She was not allowed to take her clothes, medication or other personal belongings with her.How did she win a wrongful eviction lawsuitFollowing her removal, Taylor hired an attorney and filed a lawsuit in First City Court of New Orleans on 13 January 2022. Her petition sought an injunction restoring her possession of the apartment, along with compensation for out-of-pocket expenses, inconvenience and mental anguish caused by her displacement. Under a consent agreement concerning a preliminary injunction, she was granted access to the apartment from 26 January until 16 February 2022.According to the judgment, Taylor did not remain in the apartment throughout that period. Instead, she used the time to inventory and retrieve her belongings and Ragas' possessions before leaving the premises. She placed Ragas' belongings in a storage unit, but, being unemployed, she could not maintain the payments. The storage operator eventually seized and sold the possessions. On 3 March 2025, the trial court ruled in Taylor's favour, finding that she had been wrongfully evicted and awarding her damages for mental anguish.Why did the court uphold a $1,800 wrongful eviction awardGuste Homes appealed the decision, arguing that federal law governing subsidised housing should have applied and that there was insufficient evidence to support the $1,800 award. The appeal also challenged the assessment of damages associated with conversion and mental anguish. The Fourth Circuit considered whether a property owner or manager could remove an occupant from a legally occupied property without prior notice or any court proceedings.The court acknowledged that Taylor was not a tenant under the lease but rejected the argument that this meant she could be removed without legal protection. The judgment stated: “However, under Louisiana law, occupants are afforded mandatory procedural protections similar to those of tenants.” It relied on Louisiana Code of Civil Procedure Article 4702, which requires an owner seeking to evict an occupant after the purpose of the occupancy has ended to deliver written notice allowing five days to vacate. The court also explained that the notice is only the first step in the eviction process and does not eliminate the need for court proceedings.How did emotional distress affect her wrongful eviction caseIn considering the damages, the appeal court distinguished between Taylor's mental anguish and the loss of possessions stored after the eviction. The trial court had found that Guste's actions deprived her of access to her belongings when it locked her out of the apartment. However, the judgment did not compensate her for furniture, fixtures or other items subsequently lost because she could no longer afford the storage fees. The court agreed that those material losses could not be attributed to the wrongful eviction on the facts of the case.Instead, the damages reflected the emotional distress Taylor experienced after being removed from her home. The appeal court cited the trial court’s finding that she cried frequently, was under significant stress because she had nowhere to go, and could not sleep most nights. The appeal court agreed that the manner of her removal was shocking and humiliating and found no manifest error in the trial court's assessment of general damages.The court concluded that Guste had failed to comply with the applicable procedural requirements and affirmed the original judgment. Its decision stated: “The total absence of any judicial intervention in the process is the essence of a wrongful eviction.” The $1,800 award therefore remained in place following the appeal, with the court confirming that Taylor's status as an occupant rather than the named tenant did not justify removing her without the legally required procedures.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2020, Entourage actor Adrian Grenier left Hollywood life behind and bought a 46-acre Texas ranch; he added solar power, farming and beekeeping while turning the property into a sustainable family retreat
articles.summary: Adrian Grenier, best known for playing Vincent Chase in Entourage and Nate Cooper in The Devil Wears Prada, has traded the fast-paced world of Hollywood
articles.body: Adrian Grenier, best known for playing Vincent Chase in Entourage and Nate Cooper in The Devil Wears Prada, has traded the fast-paced world of Hollywood for a quieter life on a 46-acre ranch in Texas. Since moving to Bastrop, outside Austin, in 2020, the actor has embraced sustainable living, environmental conservation and family life with his wife, Jordan Grenier, and their two children.The actor’s shift away from the entertainment industry's constant demands was not an overnight decision. After years of working in films and television, Grenier explored entrepreneurship and environmental initiatives before finding a lifestyle that allowed him to slow down and focus on what mattered most to him.Why Adrian Grenier left Hollywood for TexasGrenier first spent time in Texas in 2016 after buying a camper. During his stay, he became increasingly involved in environmental work and was drawn to the region’s relaxed atmosphere. He eventually purchased the 46-acre property that would become Kintsugi Ranch, where he has lived with his family since 2020.Speaking to PEOPLE in September 2023, Grenier explained what appealed to him about the move. “There's not a lot of social climbing, not a lot of status people. Everyone's cowboy boots and a cowboy hat, so to speak,” he said.The actor also spoke about feeling less pressure to keep up appearances than he had experienced in cities.“A lot of times in cities, I've always felt a little bit like I have to keep up with the Joneses. And here, it feels there's a lot of acceptance ... When I wake up here, I don't have anywhere to go. I'm here already,” he said.For Grenier, the move represented more than a change of address. It was an opportunity to step away from the relentless pace of celebrity life and build a more grounded routine.Inside Adrian Grenier’s sustainable ranchAt Kintsugi Ranch, Grenier has been putting his environmental beliefs into practice. The property is intended to be a sustainable family retreat, with an emphasis on living closer to nature and becoming more conscious of everyday choices. His interests include renewable energy, farming and beekeeping.Grenier told PEOPLE that he wanted the ranch to help him become “a greater steward every day in practice as a lifestyle, not just as an idea.”He has also spoken about how living closer to nature has affected his outlook on life.“You sleep better, you're more grounded, you have a sense of wellbeing,” he said, adding that the lifestyle supports mental wellbeing, resilience and practical skills. He believes it can also encourage people to make wiser decisions about how they live, treat others and care for the environment.The ranch reflects Grenier’s longstanding interest in sustainability, allowing him to incorporate environmental responsibility into his daily life rather than limiting it to advocacy.From Hollywood actor to entrepreneurGrenier’s interests have extended beyond acting for years. He has explored entrepreneurship, co-founded businesses including a microbrewery and a production company, and established a venture capital firm in 2019. In 2022, he also launched a nature-based lifestyle brand.His transition to life in Texas has not meant abandoning entertainment altogether. According to Deadline, Grenier wrapped production in Australia on the romantic comedy You, Always in December 2024. He also announced that he would host CryptoKnights, a reality series following technology entrepreneurs pitching blockchain-based startups to celebrity investors. The show premiered on Prime Video in May 2025.Rather than returning to the constant hustle of his earlier career, Grenier has spoken about wanting to use his platform in ways that feel meaningful to him.In an interview with Foundr in February 2024, he reflected on his decision to slow down and take a more deliberate approach to life.“I didn’t want to be so fast-paced and always on the go without taking time to really take in my life in the world and see how I can be of service to someone,” he said. “Like [a] ‘wake up and smell the roses’ type perspective. But this time, I’m actually growing roses.”How fatherhood changed Adrian Grenier’s prioritiesFamily has been an important part of Grenier’s decision to build a life away from Hollywood. He married Jordan Grenier in 2022 after the couple, who were first linked in 2017, spontaneously eloped during a trip to Morocco with friends.Speaking to PEOPLE, the actor described how the wedding came together unexpectedly, with their friends helping turn the moment into a celebration.Grenier and Jordan have two sons: Seiko Aurelius Grenier, born in June 2023, and Evren Saint-Eros Grenier, born in March 2025.Fatherhood also helped clarify what Grenier wanted from life. During an appearance on The Jordan B. Peterson Podcast in May 2024, he reflected on a previous separation from Jordan and his desire for a lasting partnership and family.“I didn’t want to die alone,” he said. “I wanted a family, I wanted partnership, I wanted to have children.”Life on the ranch has given Grenier the opportunity to make family time and a connection with nature central to his everyday routine.Why Adrian Grenier is not returning for The Devil Wears Prada 2Grenier’s life away from Hollywood has also kept him out of one of the most anticipated film reunions. The actor played Nate Cooper, Andy Sachs’ college boyfriend, opposite Anne Hathaway in the 2006 film The Devil Wears Prada. However, he did not return for its sequel, The Devil Wears Prada 2, which premiered in theatres on May 1, 2026.In March 2026, Grenier told PEOPLE that he had spoken to director David Frankel and was disappointed not to be included. He added that his character was controversial enough that “he might need his own spinoff.”The reaction to Nate’s character has long been a talking point among fans. In a June 2021 interview with Entertainment Weekly, Grenier admitted he had been surprised by the criticism and memes about Nate.“All those memes that came out were shocking to me,” he said. Looking back, he acknowledged that the character could be selfish and self-involved, particularly in his failure to support Andy’s career.In April 2026, Grenier also poked fun at missing out on the sequel in a Starbucks Energy Refreshers commercial. “You might have seen the headlines - I wasn’t asked to be part of a certain sequel,” he said in the advertisement. “But I’m good. Really. It’s all good energy.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Gangs in Haiti target foreign troops in the biggest attack since a new force began operations
articles.summary: Gangs in Haiti opened fire on an armored vehicle over the weekend, leaving four soldiers from El Salvador unaccounted for in the first major attack since an international gang suppression force began operations in the violence-wracked Caribbean country.
articles.body: Gangs in Haiti opened fire on an armored vehicle over the weekend, leaving four soldiers from El Salvador unaccounted for in the first major attack since an international gang suppression force began operations in the violence-wracked Caribbean country. The attack occurred Sunday in Croix-des-Bouquets, a once-peaceful community in Haiti’s capital, Port-au-Prince, that is now controlled by violent gangs. The armed forces of El Salvador said in a statement Monday that the four aviation technicians were returning to camp when their armored vehicle was attacked with explosives and set on fire. The military noted that the four men managed to flee the burning vehicle and it is working with international forces to “establish contact and determine the location of our military personnel.” Salvadoran authorities said that helicopters were dispatched to the area but they, too, came under fire as they dispersed armed men in the area. “Multiple attempts to approach by land and air have been made, but these have been hampered by the intensity of the fighting,” the Salvadoran military said. The weapons and ammunition gangs are using are not made in Haiti and will continue to find ways to enter the country, Wien-Weibert Arthus, Haiti’s deputy permanent representative to the UN, told the UN Security Council Monday. “This latest episode is a reminder, as if we really needed one, of the fact that the security challenges in Haiti are complex and complicated,” he said. “We hope that those who are missing will be able to go back to their families unscathed.” Gang violence has displaced nearly 1.5 million people, a record, across Haiti in recent years, with more than 5,700 people killed or injured from January to mid-September, and more than 230 others kidnapped, according to the UN. A warning from the U.S. Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, condemned the attack during the UN Security Council meeting on Haiti. “We believe the four men survived, but they do remain unaccounted for,” he said. “We will bring you home.” Waltz said that gangs attacked the armored vehicle with “hundreds of bullets and explosives.” “To the gangs and gang leaders who carried out this cowardly attack, if you think you’re going to intimidate this coalition into retreat, you have made a terrible mistake,” he said. The gang suppression force said in a statement that it’s assessing the situation and has advised residents where the attack occurred to remain indoors. “Gangs are testing the gang suppression force,” Jack Christofides, the force’s special representative, said at the UN Monday as he noted that attacks against the force have recently increased. He warned that gangs have carried out reprisal killings in some areas following operations by Haitian and international forces, and that they have pushed deeper into places including the community of Kenscoff and the Artibonite region. “The reality is that we cannot be everywhere at once,” Christofides said. Haiti prepares for an election despite violence The area where the armored vehicle was targeted is controlled by gangs including Chèn Méchan; Kraze Barye, led by Vitelhomme Innocent; and 400 Mawozo, led by Lanmo Sanjou. Both gang leaders have been sanctioned by the UN and the US. Romain Le Cour, head of the Haiti Observatory at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, said that while some gangs have been under pressure since the suppression force was deployed, “others want to show that they can strike back.” “If these soldiers are indeed being held, the groups gain (an) edge to negotiate and to pressure the security forces,” he said. In September 2025, the UN Security Council authorized the 5,550-member force to replace a former Kenya-led multinational force that struggled with a lack of funds and resources as it tried to help Haiti’s National Police quell gang violence. The gang suppression force has more than 2,000 troops on the ground in Haiti, including soldiers from Chad, Jamaica and Guatemala. “The force is making a difference with what it has,” Christofides said, adding that authorities have started to see early signs of reduced gang influence and control in certain areas. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack on the Salvadoran troops. It comes as Haiti prepares for its first general election in more than a decade and showcases the power of the gangs that control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince. Carlos Ruiz Massieu, the UN special envoy to Haiti, said at Monday’s meeting that electoral preparations “have reached an unprecedented level of progress.” He said that more than 35 parties and political groups have registered, along with 3,500 candidates. Among them is former Haitian President Michel Martelly, who was sanctioned in November 2022 by Canada and in August 2024 by the US, which accused him of facilitating drug trafficking and sponsoring multiple gangs.

articles.title: Timeline shows last known whereabouts of missing California woman Angelica Brophy
articles.summary: Angelica Brophy disappeared on July 6, 2026, after visiting Harrah’s Resort in Valley Center, California. Her car was found three days later at Palomar Mountain State Park near Doane Pond. The Oceanside Police Department is investigating her disappearance.
articles.body: Angelica Brophy is the baby of her family, the youngest of six children and the only girl. “She was the toughest one in the family,” older brother Ramon Fabregas said. He was 7 years old when Angelica was adopted. “It was a delight to the family. It was something new,” he told Dateline. Angelica and her siblings grew up in the Philippines and moved to California in 1990. She eventually settled with her husband, Brent, and two kids in Oceanside, a beach town near San Diego. Ramon lives north of Los Angeles and sees his little sister’s family at least once a month. In July, Ramon hosted Angelica and her family for the Fourth of July. “They drove up here and spent the weekend with us,” he said. On Monday, July 6, 44-year-old Angelica dropped her daughter off at summer camp in Oceanside around 9 a.m. She was scheduled to work a 7 p.m. shift at Kaiser Permanente, where she was a nurse. “It’s pretty natural for her,” Ramon said. “You can’t be doing nursing for all these years and not enjoy it.” He says Angelica also cared for their aging parents, even opening her home to them at one point. But that evening, Ramon got a concerning call from Angelica’s husband, Brent. Ramon says he learned that around 6 p.m. on July 6, Angelica and Brent’s son texted his father asking if he had heard from his mom. Brent called Angelica, but got no answer. He drove to her workplace to see if she would arrive for her 7 p.m. shift. She never showed up. Brent reported his wife missing that night. A press release from the Oceanside Police Department (OPD) confirms that Angelica was reported missing “at approximately 9:30 p.m.” The press release states, “The following day, the Investigations Division of the police department began following up on leads to locate Brophy.” Angelica’s family quickly sprang into action to search for her and spread the word on social media. Ramon drove down to Oceanside. “My focus was solely to be there for the kids,” he said. Dateline spoke with Lisa Fabregas, who is married to Angelica’s brother Martin. The couple was at home in Toronto when they learned from Ramon that Angelica was missing. “I checked everything. I sent messages out to her on Facebook, on WhatsApp, even sent a regular text,” Lisa said. “I tried calling her phone. Martin did the same thing. Nothing.” The Fabregas family was flooded with Facebook messages offering help and others fueling speculation. Within days of Angelica’s disappearance, they created a website to centralize the facts. “Anything that we put in the website, we were able to verify with the police first,” Lisa said. “We didn’t want to hamper their investigation at all in any way, shape, or form.” Using surveillance footage and bank transactions, investigators were able to piece together a timeline of Angelica’s last known movements. “Brophy’s last known location was Harrah’s Resort in Valley Center on July 6, 2026, at approximately 3:30 pm.,” an OPD press release states. Her family says Angelica regularly visited the casino at Harrah’s Resort. “Approximately 50 minutes later, Brophy entered Palomar Mountain State Park after purchasing a parking ticket from park staff,” the press release continues. The state park is about an hour from Oceanside. The Oceanside Police Department also “contacted Brophy’s cell phone carrier and ‘pinged’ her phone,” according to the press release. “The ping was unable to provide any information because Brophy’s phone was either turned off or its battery was dead.” Lisa says her sister-in-law was a frequent hiker who explored trails “all around the San Diego area with her friends.” She says Angelica had been to that state park before. Three days after Angelica vanished, her car was found in a parking lot in Palomar Mountain State Park near Doane Pond. “However, Brophy was not with her vehicle,” the OPD stated in its release. According to Lisa, the car was locked, and Angelica’s phone, wallet, and passport were found inside. “Officers with the California State Parks, supported by the San Diego County Sheriff’s Department’s Search and Rescue team, began searching for Brophy,” the press release states, noting that the operations spanned many hours over multiple days. “Despite their best efforts, the search-and-rescue teams were unable to locate Brophy.” Ramon says he led most of the community searches for Angelica in the months after she disappeared. “The support from the nurses and her friends at work have been amazing,” he said, adding that dozens of volunteers showed up every day to help look for his sister. “It’s been an outpouring of support.” Click on the image below to look at an interactive map of the search efforts: Lisa and her husband flew out to California as soon as they could. “We went out in groups and started hiking and searching for her,” she said. “There have been so many people and so many volunteer organizations that have come forward.” Despite the extensive search efforts, Angelica remains missing. In the OPD’s July 22 press release on Angelica’s case, Chief Taurino Valdovino said, “I want to emphasize that there is still no evidence of foul play in this case. However, we will continue to work closely with the Brophy family to locate Angelica.” Dateline reached out to the Oceanside Police Department for an interview and was told by email it “will not provide interviews, offer additional comments, or release any further information” in the case “beyond what has already been publicly released.” Angelica’s brothers and their families have joined forces to field media requests and work with OPD. Lisa says they are trying to help Brent and his children “live their lives peacefully” as they deal with Angelica’s disappearance. Lisa misses her sister-in-law. “I promised her, you know, that I would take care of her,” she said. “I miss her laughs. I miss that she can’t sing to save her life.” Angelica’s loved ones shared a plea on the family’s website, writing: “Her loving husband and kids need her home safe, and are desperate for life to feel normal again. Her patients need the warm and vigilant care she provides in their own most vulnerable moments and times of need. And the rest of us need her infectious smile and unmistakable laugh back in our lives. There are more memories to be made with her friends and family, and we need that support from our community more than ever.” Ramon has a more direct appeal to the public. “We’re trying to reach someone that knows something or overheard something,” he said. “We don’t know yet the circumstances of her disappearance. So that’s -- that’s what we’re pleading for. If there’s anyone that could help us or knows something, just one phone call, you know, can lead us to her and to get her home.” Angelica is 5’5”, 130 lbs. She has dark brown hair and brown eyes. She was last seen wearing black leggings, a light gray pullover, and white sneakers. She may have been carrying a blue and pink pineapple backpack. Anyone with information is encouraged to contact Oceanside Police Detective Ryan Malone at 760-435-4537 or the anonymous tip line at 760-435-4730. Angelica’s family has also set up a phone line for information and can be reached at 619-377-8399. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: Trump approval hits record-low 31 percent, polls show Republican struggles
articles.summary: Reuters/Ipsos poll shows Democrats leading by 12 points in generic US congressional ballot surveys against Republicans.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 31 percent – another record low in his political career, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll.

The same poll found Trump’s Republican Party also at a major disadvantage: when respondents were asked whether they would rather vote for a generic, unnamed Democrat or Republican, Democrats led by 12 points.

The percentage of Americans who disapprove of Trump has grown steadily in recent months, especially since the February 28 launch of the US-Israel war on Iran, which has driven up petrol and diesel prices and had knock-on effects across the economy.

Several recent polls have documented the growing problems facing Trump and his party ahead of midterm elections, set for November 3, which could determine control of the House and Senate.

An NBC poll released Sunday found 71 percent of Americans said the country was on the “wrong track” and 55 percent would vote for the Democratic Party if an election were held that day.

A Washington Post/ABC/Ipsos poll, also released on Monday, found Trump had a record-low approval rating of 33 percent, with 7 out of 10 saying petrol or gasoline was becoming unaffordable.

articles.title: Famed wedding venue of Michael Douglas, others closing for years, leaving brides scrambling
articles.summary: The famed Plaza Hotel in New York City will close for at least four years starting January 2027, leaving couples scrambling to find new wedding venues.
articles.body: One of New York City's most storied hotels is shutting its doors for years, leaving brides and grooms scrambling to secure new wedding venues. For over a century, The Plaza Hotel in Manhattan has stood as the ultimate crown jewel of luxury weddings, setting the stage for extravagant celebrations — most notably the star-studded 2000 nuptials of Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones and a glamorous gathering back in 1968 for Julie Nixon and David Eisenhower. The Fifth Avenue landmark is also deeply woven into the fabric of popular culture. It has served as the backdrop for blockbuster films like "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York" and "Bride Wars." LUXURY HOTEL FAVORED BY KENNEDYS, GRACE KELLY CRACKS DOWN ON INFLUENCER PHOTO SHOOTS It was also the beloved stomping ground of Eloise from Kay Thompson's classic children’s books. The Plaza Hotel will close in January 2027 for at least four years as the landmark undergoes extensive restoration work, the hotel said in a press release shared with Fox News Digital. The hotel, which opened in 1907 overlooking Central Park, said the work will focus on repairing and restoring its historic façade. "Due to the complexity of this undertaking and significant intrusion to operations, The Plaza Hotel will be closing for at least four years commencing January 2027 while the work is underway," the hotel said. The announced closure is creating uncertainty for couples who had planned to marry at the hotel. Christine Carney, 38, had planned a roughly 200-person wedding at the Plaza for May 1 after booking the venue nearly a year in advance, the outlet reported. Carney told the Post she learned about the closure from a friend rather than the hotel itself, leaving her worried about the money already paid for her wedding. "I'm definitely frustrated and disappointed that this happened, and I'm anxious to figure out what the next steps will be," she told the outlet. articles.title: Mississippi AG says police shooting that killed 1-year-old was ‘justified’
articles.summary: Kohen Wiley was killed in June when officers fired at a car at a Walmart parking lot. A friend of Wiley’s mother, who was driving the car, was injured.
articles.body: The fatal shooting of a 1-year-old by a Mississippi police officer who fired at a vehicle while responding to a shoplifting call was a “justified” use of force, the state attorney general said Monday. Attorney General Lynn Fitch’s office issued the brief statement four months after Kohen Wiley was killed when an officer shot at a car that police said was fleeing from a Walmart parking lot in Senatobia. “Today, the Office of the Attorney General announced it has completed the review of a June 14, 2026, incident in Senatobia involving one officer with the Senatobia Police Department,” the AG’s office said in the statement. “In this incident, the Attorney General’s Office found the use of force was justified.” The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation conducted the investigation. In a statement, an attorney for Wiley’s family questioned the investigation’s conclusions and urged the department to release body camera video from the shooting. “If the footage supports the state’s decision, release it,” Ben Crump said in the statement. “We will not stop fighting until this family gets the truth.” There was no immediate response from Wiley’s family, which has for months been taking part in protests demanding justice for the slain boy in the small town 40 miles south of Memphis, Tennessee. The shooting happened after the responding officers arrived at Walmart and saw “two subjects and a juvenile child fleeing from the store into a vehicle,” the MBI said. Kohen’s mother, whom her lawyer identified as Vellesiya Wiley, was a passenger. Her friend was driving. “Officers attempted to stop the vehicle, but the driver drove in the direction of the officers, almost striking one,” the MBI said in a June 14 report. “An officer then discharged their weapon and the vehicle fled the scene. The subjects arrived at a local hospital where one juvenile child in the vehicle was pronounced deceased, and another subject had critical injuries.” Kohen’s mother has disputed that account. In a video Crump posted on social media in June, Wiley said they had gone to Walmart for diapers. She said that her friend was briefly stopped while they were leaving the store and that “I kept walking because it had nothing to do with me.” “By the time me and my baby got in the car, she came,” Wiley said of her friend. They encountered police as they began to back out, Wiley said. “I raised my baby up trying to show them that he was in the car,” she said. In that moment, Wiley’s friend inadvertently hit another car while Wiley’s door was open. Wiley said her friend did not try to hit the officers. “They was all on the right side, and she was driving towards the left,” she said. In July, the family’s lawyers, Crump and Van Turner, released a preliminary autopsy report that they contend showed that the bullet that killed the child and wounded the driver was fired through one side of the car, fueling fresh questions about whether the shooting was justified. “His mother, who has not been charged with any crime, says she was trying to communicate to officers that there was a baby in the car,” Crump said.

articles.title: 160 people reported killed in escalating drone attacks across Sudan
articles.summary: Rights groups warn increasing attacks by unmanned aircraft are targeting civilians and infrastructure.
articles.body:
A wave of drone attacks across Sudan has killed more than 160 people in recent days, according to medics and rights groups.

D rone attacks on Khartoum killed three children on Monday, according to Emergency Lawyers, a group that monitors violence against civilians in Sudan’s civil war, while more than 160 were reported to have been killed in western regions since Friday.

The attacks were blamed on both the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and government forces, They have been fighting since 2023, but the increasing use of drones in recent months has caused growing numbers of civilian casualties.

The deadliest recent attack was near a market on Sunday evening in Al-Dibab town in the southwestern state of West Kordofan, which is controlled by the RSF. Residents and medical workers said a drone attacked a transport hub where villagers had gathered after a market day to find rides home, killing 80 people.

Another 47 wounded people were taken to the nearby town of Al-Mujlad, where 30 later died from their injuries, a medical source said, according to the AFP news agency.

The RSF’s self-declared administration, known as Tasis, and Emergency Lawyers accused the army of carrying out the attack.

In eastern Sudan, a military source said on Sunday that air defences intercepted several RSF drones targeting the Atbara and Setit dams in Gadaref state, about 420km east of Khartoum. There was no immediate comment from the RSF.

Early on Monday, another drone attack hit the RSF stronghold of Nyala, the capital of South Darfur. Medical and RSF sources said 17 people, including seven RSF officers, were killed and 23 wounded.

An RSF drone attack on Friday hit a gathering of displaced people in Sudan’s Blue Nile province on the border with Ethiopia, killing 41 people, Emergency Lawyers said.

The group condemned the attack, calling it a humanitarian tragedy.

The United Nations condemned the deadly attacks on Monday.

“We are alarmed by the continued deadly drone strikes across the country that are killing civilians, including children, and that are disrupting central services,” Stephane Dujarric, spokesperson for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, told reporters.

The current war in Sudan began in April 2023 when the military leader, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, also known as Hemedti, fell out over plans to fold the paramilitary into Sudan’s army.

In June, Hemedti was sentenced to death in his absence for war crimes.

However, the fighting, now in its fourth year, continues and has killed at least 59,000 people, according to conflict monitor ACLED. Aid groups say the actual toll is likely higher.

The UN says about 13 million people have been forced from their homes, creating what aid groups call the world’s largest humanitarian crisis.

Across Sudan, 33.7 million people, including 17.3 million children, urgently need food support this year. An estimated 825,000 children face severe, acute malnutrition, according to the UN.

The United States on Friday urged the UN Security Council to push for a humanitarian truce and expand an arms embargo on Sudan, but China and Russia opposed widening the embargo.
